item.title: Kyoto's iconic autumn foliage draws crowds of visitors
item.description: Tourists flock to Kyoto, Japan, to admire vibrant autumn foliage as red, orange and golden maple leaves transform the former imperial capital.

item.title: Civilian flights diverted as Kuwait army intercepts Iranian drone attack
item.description: Kuwait's military said four people were injured after "a number of hostile" Iranian drones were detected and intercepted in its airspace. Flights crossing Iraq toward the Gulf were given new headings ahead of Kuwait, shifting the international corridor.

item.title: Fathers' antidepressant use tied to slight blood pressure risk in kids — but drugs may not be why
item.description: Researchers said their findings should offer reassurance for hopeful fathers who take antidepressants.

item.title: Farmers demonstrate in Brussels against EU budget cuts
item.description: Francie Gorman, President of the Irish Farmers Association, warns that cuts to the common agricultural policy could threaten their livelihoods, food security and the future of European farming.

item.title: Judges in Netanyahu corruption trial urges dropping key charges
item.description: Israel continues to struggle to form a government after the 27 October election. Netanyahu has denied wrongdoing in all three cases since his trial began in May 2020.

item.title: Ashes to ashes: FC Barcelona reveals plans to let Camp Nou be fans' final resting place
item.description: Extra-time may soon have a different meaning for fans of FC Barcelona. Supporters are now being offered the chance to keep their ashes at the Spanish football club, under recently announced plans to build a memorial within the walls of the famous Camp Nou stadium.

item.title: Watch as rare cloud 'waterfall' cascades over Christ the Redeemer in Rio de Janeiro
item.description: The natural phenomenon went viral on social media, forcing photographers to confirm that it wasn't produced by artificial intelligence.

item.title: TUI boss wants EU to cut bureaucracy, attract talent and expand green energy
item.description: Euronews spoke with TUI's CEO Sebastian Ebel about manure-powered cruise ships, migration, dependence on the US, Artificial Intelligence, and the future of tourism.

item.title: Norwegian low-cost carrier Norse Atlantic suspends flights as bankruptcy looms
item.description: Norwegian low-cost carrier Norse Atlantic, hit by surging jet fuel prices due to the war against Iran, said on Thursday that it was teetering on the verge of bankruptcy as it cancelled all flights for the day.

item.title: Flames and thick smoke billow from Bangkok oil facility after massive explosion
item.description: A powerful explosion rocks an oil depot in Bangkok, Thailand, sending thick black smoke into the sky and prompting evacuation warnings.

item.title: Feminists march across Spain against violence ahead of general election
item.description: Demonstrations for the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women come just days before elections in which the far right could approach 20% of the vote.

item.title: ‘The taste layer of the internet ’: Reddit's COO on why AI needs humans
item.description: Euronews Next spoke to Jen Wong about the threat of AI to the open internet and the importance of human connection on the platform.

item.title: From Vice City to gaming suites: How Grand Theft Auto VI is changing the way people travel
item.description: From hotels with dedicated gaming rooms to real-life destinations featured in blockbuster titles, video games are increasingly influencing holiday plans. New data reveals a surge in searches for gaming-themed stays, with the release of Grand Theft Auto VI helping fuel the trend.

item.title: Images show Kim Jong Un inspecting North Korean nuclear facilities
item.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has called for expanding the country's nuclear arsenal after visiting nuclear material production facilities and a weapons research institute.

item.title: Why the Mediterranean is a hotspot for oil spills after tanker sinks near Ibiza
item.description: Any pollution entering the water could have a possible impact on Mediterranean seagrasses that absorb substantial quantities of climate-heating carbon dioxide.

item.title: Musk says will give two SpaceX shares to 'every child in America'
item.description: Tech billionaire Elon Musk said on Wednesday he would give every child in the United States two shares in his SpaceX rocket company, doubling an offer he made last month.

item.title: EU must find new revenue or scale back spending plans, MEP says
item.description: EU leaders are meeting in Brussels to discuss the bloc’s next seven-year budget.

item.title: US says SpaceX can deploy 1 million satellites to build data centres in space
item.description: The US Federal Communications Commission authorised Elon Musk's rocket company to create a data centre constellation to power AI on earth.

item.title: After initial reluctance, Bulgaria says it's 'ready' to join €45 billion Ukraine loan
item.description: Bulgaria will contribute to the new €45 billion support loan to Ukraine, Prime Minister Rumen Radev confirmed on Thursday. But the country will not help pay for weapons and ammunition.

item.title: Less sex, more screens: Britain’s sexual habits are changing
item.description: One in three 16- to 24-year-olds have never had sex, up from one in five in 2010.

item.title: UK sent Sri Lankan refugee to Eswatini in secret deal, the BBC says
item.description: The United Kingdom reportedly sent a Sri Lankan refugee who had been convicted of sexual assault to Eswatini, where he committed suicide, as part of a secret deal, according to an investigation by the BBC.

item.title: Cheaper, generic HIV prevention drug arrives in Zambia
item.description: The rollout in Zambia is part of a plan to ensure people in lower-income countries can access the breakthrough HIV prevention drug.

item.title: Ebola cases in Congo surpass 12,000 in fastest-growing outbreak
item.description: The ongoing outbreak is the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history.

item.title: New Danish data breach hits 11,000 despite security upgrades
item.description: The latest incident comes despite Denmark upgrading its cybersecurity systems after an earlier breach exposed data linked to millions of people.

item.title: Nuclear explosion in space would create 'a huge bell of radiation' to stay for months, says expert
item.description: Florence Duvellier, military fellow at the Defense Unit of the Security Studies Center at the French Institute for International Relations in Paris, says a nuclear explosion in space by Russia is "technically possible" but also a means to "stay as a big space power".

item.title: Wreckage and burnt vehicles as fuel tanker fire kills 31 on Cairo highway
item.description: A massive fire from a fuel tanker crash on Giza’s Ring Road in Waraq killed at least 31 and injured 21, highlighting Egypt’s deadly road risks.

item.title: Huge explosion at Bangkok oil depot sends black smoke over Thai capital
item.description: A major explosion at a Bangchak oil facility in eastern Bangkok sent flames and thick black smoke into the sky on Thursday. Authorities urged people living nearby to evacuate as emergency services responded to the incident.

item.title: Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt settle long-running legal battle over French winery
item.description: Ownership of Château Miraval, a prestigious estate in the Var, France, was one of the main points of contention in Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie’s divorce.

item.title: Trump thanks Uzbekistan for traditional pavilions gifted to Washington park
item.description: Crafted from the wood of 200-year-old walnut trees, the structures stand near some of Washington's best-known monuments. The gift commemorates the independence anniversaries of both countries.

item.title: New images show stadium-sized crater on asteroid NASA crashed into
item.description: Europe's Hera spacecraft has released its first close-up footage of Dimorphos, four years after NASA deliberately smashed a probe into it.

item.title: Do heat pumps actually work in cold weather? Expert reveals how the technology copes at -20°C
item.description: Heat pumps are becoming increasingly popular amid spiralling gas prices, but can the green technology survive a freezing winter?

item.title: Christmas 2026 travel gift guide: Perfect presents for people who love travelling
item.description: If you’re making a list and checking it twice, then don’t forget to add in some of the travel gift options from our round-up.

item.title: Inquiry into UK nuclear test veterans granted after 40 year campaign
item.description: Veterans say they were effectively used as test subjects, with some exposed to radioactive fallout without adequate protection.

item.title: EU wants more data centres but won't force new green commitments, leaked draft reveals
item.description: The EU is preparing a voluntary agreement to accelerate data centre expansion as it seeks to triple capacity within five to seven years, despite growing concerns about electricity consumption and pressure on power grids.

item.title: Duran Duran pays tribute to guitarist Andy Taylor, dead at 65 after battle with prostate cancer
item.description: Taylor died "following a long and courageous battle with prostate cancer", the band announced.

item.title: Kabul's balloon sellers turn hardship into moments of joy
item.description: Amid Kabul’s busy streets, Shamsuddin and Omran sell up to 700 colourful balloons a day, turning memories of war and poverty into moments of joy.

item.title: UniCredit secures final Polish approval for Commerzbank takeover bid
item.description: KNF's approval completes the authorisation process for the Commerzbank deal. Governance, the German public stake and the next stages of the offer still need to be defined.

item.title: Greece creates 20 free day centres for dementia patients and caregivers
item.description: Greece is opening 20 new day centres for people with Alzheimer’s disease and other forms of dementia.

item.title: Ship transporting 7,000 tonnes of diesel sinks off Ibiza, one crewman dead
item.description: The other 16 crew members are reported to have survived. The authorities have activated emergency plans and are monitoring the risk of marine pollution.

item.title: Europe’s €2 trillion punch-up: Welcome to the Brussels fight club
item.description: Good morning. Leo Cendrowicz here with your Thursday newsletter. We have almighty punch-up on our agenda today, as EU leaders gather in Brussels to brawl over their seven-year budget – a slugfest that almost certainly won’t be resolved by the end of the summit.

item.title: Gaudí's dying wish: New documents reveal Spanish architect's final gift to Sagrada Família
item.description: The inventory of Antoni Gaudí's estate reveals that the legendary Spanish architect wished to devote all his assets, including his Parc Güell house and his savings, to financing the works of the iconic Sagrada Família.

item.title: King tides and powerful waves destroy pier and flood homes in California
item.description: King tides and powerful waves destroy part of Pacifica's pier and flood coastal homes in California, US, prompting warnings from authorities.

item.title: Three Iberian cities in Europe's 2027 top 10 for property investors
item.description: According to global property consultancy Colliers' 2027 report, Madrid, Lisbon and Barcelona rank among the ten European cities most sought after by property investors, as people in Spain and Portugal protest over the cost of housing.

item.title: Europe Today: EU leaders in Brussels for budget talks and Latvian PM Kulbergs on Euronews
item.description: The EU’s 27 heads of state are meeting in Brussels for a European Council summit, which some are forecasting to be a long-term budget bust-up like no other. We speak with the Latvian prime minister Andris Kulbergs.

item.title: EU summit: Budget deal 'light years away', Meloni says as talks continue
item.description: EU leaders are set to clash over the next EU budget and future support for Ukraine at a crucial summit in Brussels.

item.title: UK discounter Poundland enters administration with 11,000 jobs at risk
item.description: The collapse of Poundland marks another major setback for Britain's struggling retail sector, which has been hit by weak consumer spending, rising costs and fierce competition.

item.title: Doomsday fears are fuelling panic-buying. Could it worsen global food waste?
item.description: As fears of a global conflict drive consumers to stockpile supplies, experts warn that panic-buying could lead to food waste, shortages and price hikes.

item.description: From Pacific island nations where flights come weekly to a little-visited part of Europe, here’s where to head when you’re looking to visit a place none of your friends have been.
